sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the federal bribery statute. It asks if a public official commits a crime by merely arranging access to government agencies. the side that brought the case argues this conduct is not an official act. The government argues it is.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The outcome defines the boundary between lawful advocacy and criminal bribery. It determines whether arranging meetings constitutes a specific government action. This standard affects all public officials nationwide. It shapes the legal definition of official conduct.
